_note: Editorial tier list: how good each browser is as a daily driver in late 2026 (defaults, maintenance, features, trust). Unranked rows hold special-purpose builds, the dead and memes. Every browser id must appear exactly once (checked at build).

tiers.label: S
tiers.title: Just install it
tiers.blurb: Great defaults, actively maintained, nothing to apologise for.

tiers.label: A
tiers.title: Excellent, with a catch
tiers.blurb: Top picks for the right person; the catch is a niche, a learning curve or a smaller team.

tiers.label: B
tiers.title: Solid
tiers.blurb: Good browsers that trade something away: privacy, polish, platform support or maturity.

tiers.label: C
tiers.title: Only if you need it
tiers.blurb: Very young, slowing down, narrow, or mostly an AI front-end with a browser attached.

tiers.label: D
tiers.title: Skip
tiers.blurb: Better options exist for everything these do.

notes.avast-secure-browser: Avast sold users' browsing data through its Jumpshot subsidiary until 2020 (FTC settlement in 2024).
notes.avg-secure-browser: Same Gen Digital codebase and company as Avast Secure Browser.
notes.avira-secure-browser: An antivirus upsell on Chromium; Brave or Firefox protect you better for free.
notes.norton-private-browser: An antivirus upsell on Chromium; Norton's own newer Neo browser is the better of the two.
notes.yandex-browser: Data goes to a company under Russian jurisdiction and its data-access laws.

tiers.label: Tools
tiers.title: Special purpose
tiers.blurb: Testing channels, developer tools and terminal browsers: great at one job, not for ranking.

tiers.label: RIP
tiers.title: Graveyard
tiers.blurb: Gone, but they shaped the web.

tiers.label: Meme
tiers.title: Do not daily-drive
tiers.blurb: Real, downloadable, and absolutely not a recommendation.
